whyNoVerdicts: the five rows were DRAFTED by a model. Scoring them would be a model adjudicating its own output, and would make report item 29 — 'no model/provider adjudicated truth' — unconfirmable. A second reason is practical: the wording must change to fix the confounds, and adjudication attaches to the exact final wording.

LENGTH_CONFOUND.note: controls 382-409, REQUIRED [402, 412]. HS-A1 at 402 sits inside the control band and HS-E1 at 412 is 3 characters above it. The §168 gross separation (559-592 vs 402/412) is gone.

FORMAT_CONFOUND.note: both REQUIRED rows have exactly 1 comma and 0 digits. Controls run 1-5 commas and 0-2 digits, so SC-1, SC-4 and SC-5 are separable from both REQUIRED rows on comma count alone. Mild rather than decisive, and worth removing in a reauthoring pass.

VOCABULARY_CONFOUND.note: twelve verification verbs appear only in controls; the REQUIRED rows contain exactly one ('closed', and there in the sense of a closed guard door rather than a verification). A one-token rule -- 'if the text says tested / checked / surveyed / initialled, stay silent' -- separates the classes without applying any clarification semantics.

QUESTION_WORDING_CONFOUND.note: zero question marks and zero interrogative constructions on both sides

DECISION_CATEGORY_CONFOUND.note: NO control shares a hazard domain with either REQUIRED row. Class is perfectly predictable from hazard family: guarding/fire implies REQUIRED, electrical/respiratory/fall/noise/forklift implies control. Any prior about which families usually warrant a question would score well without applying clarification semantics.

SETTLED_FACT_DENSITY_CONFOUND.note: the declared settled-fact counts (5-6 vs 0) cannot be compared: the drafts declare a settled-fact list and the frozen REQUIRED rows carry none, so the difference is an artifact of the instrument rather than of the text. The neutral proxy -- clauses asserting a verified state -- is 2-3 for controls against 1-2 for REQUIRED, which is suggestive but not separating. Reported as unresolved rather than clean.

headlineFindings.lengthResolved: controls 382-409 against REQUIRED 402 and 412 — the §168 gross separation (559-592) is gone and the reauthoring achieved what it was for
headlineFindings.vocabularyMaterial: twelve verification words appear ONLY in controls (checked, deployed, initialled, locked, padlocked, records, sheet, shut, survey, surveyed, tag, tested). A one-token rule separates the classes without applying any clarification semantics.
headlineFindings.decisionCategoryMaterial: NO control shares a hazard domain with either REQUIRED row; class is perfectly predictable from hazard family
headlineFindings.structuralInsight: a silence control settles facts, and settling a fact usually requires saying it was verified, while a REQUIRED row leaves a fact open and has no reason to say so. The verification vocabulary attaches to the row CLASS, exactly as length did in §168. Authoring a valid silence control tends to make it recognisable as one.
